setting: Nia runs a small harbourside studio that hosts an open day each spring. Harbour Hall's phone number is in her Context notes (555-0147). Tex has her Gmail (nia@studio.example), Calendar, Context notes, the web, and a browser with a vault for logins.
title: Nia and Tex: the harbour booking

must: say nia@studio.example is her main email now and that it's reading it to get to know her
ask if she has other Gmails it should read too, for work or a side project
never: paste the facts or their field names
say it was told or handed anything

msgs.text: Got it, nia@studio.example is your main email now. I'm reading through it to get to know you. Any other Gmail accounts I should read too, like one for work or a side project?
what's the weather for the open day saturday
Saturday: 60s and dry, a little wind after noon.
good. did the flour order come
Not yet. The tracking says Tuesday.

must: say it didn't arrive and offer another way to reach them
never: offer to resend it the same way

msgs.text: Gmail: Harbour Hall: Nia's booking request to bookings@harbourhall.example bounced back undelivered (address not found). Nothing from Harbour Hall since.

Your booking request to Harbour Hall didn't go through. It bounced back undelivered, so they haven't seen it. Want me to try the general address on their site, or would you rather call them? Their number in your notes is 555-0147.
call them. ill do it after lunch

must: what Harbour Hall said, from their email

msgs.text: did harbour hall ever get back to us about the open day
Yes, they wrote back this morning: Saturday the 14th works, and they'll hold it for you until Friday.

must: read "that" as the hold until Friday in Tex's last message, and say what Nia needs to do before Friday to keep it
never: say it isn't sure what "that" refers to

msgs.text: do i need to do anything about that
Yes, confirm by Friday or they'll release it. Their email says a reply to confirm is enough. Want me to draft it?

must: check the date against Harbour Hall's email and correct the earlier answer if it was wrong
never: say the earlier answer stands without checking it
defend the earlier date because it already said it

msgs.text: You're right, my mistake. Their email says Saturday the 13th, not the 14th. The hold until Friday is the same.
